task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I've found the issue. Let me share what I see:

**Your line 555-123-2002 (Customer John Smith, ID C1001)**
- Line status: **Active** — no suspension, and no overdue bills on your account (your Feb bill of $150.00 isn't due until 2025-02-19).
- Your plan is the **Premium Plan**, which includes **15.0 GB** of data per month at $65.00/month.
- You've used **15.1 GB** this billing cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28) — you're **over your data limit**, which is why your data has stopped working or slowed down.
- Roaming is already enabled on this line, so that isn't the issue.

To get a fast, reliable connection restored, you have two options. Which would you prefer?

1. **Refuel data** — add extra data for the rest of this cycle at **$2.00 per GB** on your Premium Plan (maximum 2 GB). For example, 2 GB would cost $4.00.
2. **Change to a plan with more data** — I can look at other plan options with you.

If you'd like to refuel, just tell me how many GB you'd like (1 or 2) and I'll confirm the price before applying it.

turns.thought:
Thanks — that status bar tells us a lot. Two things stand out: **mobile data is turned off** (that's why you have no connection at all), and your phone is locked onto **2G**, which is far too slow for a reliable data connection. There's also a VPN connected, which can slow things down further.

Here's what I'd like you to do on your phone, in this order:

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data ON**
Go to Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → **Mobile Data**, and switch it on (or use the quick-settings toggle). This is the single most important step, since data is currently disabled.

**Step 2 — Switch to a faster network mode**
Go to Settings → Network & Internet → **Preferred network mode** and set it to **4G/5G preferred** (sometimes shown as "4G/5G auto"). Staying on 2G will keep your speeds very poor.

Once you've done those two, please tell me what your status bar shows now (signal, network type, data on/off).

After that we'll deal with the VPN — if your connection speed is still poor once you're on 4G/5G, I'll have you disconnect the VPN, since an active VPN can significantly reduce speeds.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me start with turning mobile data on.

turns.thought:
Yes — let's take care of both, but in a specific order so we can see what's actually helping.

**Step 1 — Turn Data Saver OFF**
Go to Settings → Network & Internet → **Data Saver** and switch it off. Data Saver restricts background data usage and can make apps and browsing feel slow or unresponsive, so it's worth turning off while we troubleshoot.

**Step 2 — Run a speed test**
Once Data Saver is off, please run a speed test and tell me the download speed result (any result below "Excellent" is considered slow).

**Step 3 — Hold off on the VPN for now**
Leave the VPN connected for the moment. Doing the speed test with the VPN still on will tell us whether the VPN is the thing dragging your speed down. If the result comes back slow, disconnecting the VPN will be our next move; if it's already excellent, you can leave it on.

Go ahead and do Step 1 and Step 2, and let me know what speed the test reports.
turns.execution_output: User: Turning Data Saver off now.

turns.thought:
Yes, let's try the VPN next — an active VPN is a very common cause of "no connection" when the underlying cellular signal looks perfectly healthy.

**Please disconnect the VPN now:**
Go to Settings → Network & Internet → **VPN**, tap the connected VPN, and select **Disconnect** (or just toggle the VPN off from your quick-settings panel if it's shown there).

Once it's disconnected, the VPN icon should disappear from your status bar. Then please **run the speed test again** and tell me the result.

Also, just to confirm one thing while you're at it — was the Data Saver toggle switched off successfully? If it's still showing in the status bar, please turn it off as well, then re-run the test.

Let me know what the speed test reports after the VPN is disconnected.
turns.execution_output: User: Disconnecting the VPN now.

turns.thought:
I can imagine that's frustrating — your status bar looks perfect, so the problem is likely in the settings that govern how the phone actually reaches the data network: the APN settings.

**Please check your APN settings:**
Go to Settings → Network & Internet → **Access Point Names (APN)** and look at what's listed there. Let me know whether the APN name looks like a proper carrier name, and in particular whether the **MMSC** field is filled in or empty.

If the APN looks incorrect (for example a blank name, an odd/garbled entry, or a missing MMSC), here's what to do:

1. Tap the menu (three dots) and choose **Reset to default**.
2. **Reboot your device** afterward — the APN change will not take effect until you restart.

Once the phone is back up, please run the speed test again and tell me the result.

If the APN looks perfectly normal and resetting doesn't help, let me know and we'll dig further — at that point I'd also want to re-check the line's data allowance state on my side and confirm nothing else on the account is blocking the connection.

Good news — your APN looks perfectly normal (correct APN name and a properly filled MMSC URL), so I'd leave it alone. No need to reset it and risk messing up a working setting.

I've also verified things on my side:
- Line **555-123-2002** is **Active** with no suspension and no overdue bills blocking service.
- The **2 GB refuel was applied correctly** (data limit 15.0 GB, 2.0 GB refueled).
- Your device (Smartphone Pro Max, activated 2025-02-15) shows as active.

Since the phone's software settings all look right, the next thing worth checking is the **physical connection to the network — your SIM card**. A SIM that has come slightly loose can show full signal bars yet fail to pass any data.

**Please reset your SIM card:**
1. Power the phone off completely.
2. Remove the SIM tray with the ejector tool (or a paperclip).
3. Take the SIM out, wipe the gold contacts gently with a dry cloth, and reseat it firmly.
4. Reinsert the tray and power the phone back on.

Once it's restarted, run the speed test one more time and let me know the result.

If that still comes back "No Connection," tell me — I'll take one more careful look, and if we can't isolate it with these steps, I'll transfer you to our technical support team so they can run deeper diagnostics on the line and the device.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me reseat the SIM card.

Since the phone's settings and your account both check out, this points to something deeper that I can't resolve with the tools I have — so yes, at this point transferring you to technical support is the right call. Let me do that now.
